title: Model entry profiles, soft‑pin lifecycle, and compatibility rubric for community weights
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Clarify the concrete requirements for accepting new open/community model weights into the Redwood model catalog, with an emphasis on: (1) a small set of entry profiles that map model artifacts to runtime capability targets, (2) a documented soft‑pin lifecycle to enable staged exposure and safe rollbacks, and (3) a compatibility rubric that runtime and ops teams can use to determine supported optimizations (quantization tiers, KV cache semantics, attention kernels). This ticket captures product decisions, acceptance criteria, and concrete artifacts the onboarding flow must require of upstream contributors.
scope_changes: Initial intake will only require metadata and basic smoke tests for Tier-0 and Tier-1 profiles. Tier-2/Tier-3 profiles (heavy optimization targets) are out of scope for the first rollout and will be tracked as follow-ups. We will not require SSO/provenance signatures for ephemeral community variants in this phase — those will be added in the next compliance sprint.
risks:
- Misclassification of profile could lead to runtime failures when optimizations are applied.
- Overly strict pin rules may block high-quality community submissions.
- Lack of clear fallback mapping could increase error rates for Private deployments with pinned versions.
implementation_notes: Product will publish the profile matrix and the minimal manifest schema (model_manifest v1). Eng will implement an ingestion validator that verifies manifest fields and runs a lightweight runtime signature probe. Ops will add telemetry tags for catalog_profile to help post-release monitoring. Plan: design->eng spike (2w)->ingest validator (ENG)->console UX for profile selection (PM+DES)->canary soft‑pin rollout (ops).
acceptance_criteria: A1: A formal profile matrix (Tier-0..Tier-3) exists in Confluence with deterministic rules for classification based on architecture, tokenizer type, and opset surface.

A2: model_manifest v1 schema is published and includes: architecture identifier, tokenizer spec (BPE/Unigram/other), expected opset list, quantization candidate tiers, provided smoke test suite hash, and declared provenance link.
A3: Ingestion validator implemented to reject manifests missing required fields for the chosen profile and to emit clear failure codes for contributors.

A4: Soft‑pin lifecycle defined and implemented in catalog UI/metadata with phases: trial -> soft-pinned -> pinned -> deprecated; each phase has explicit metrics and duration defaults (trial=7d, soft-pinned=14d).
A5: Compatibility rubric exists that maps runtime features (KV cache safe, token streaming, flash-attention safe) to profile tiers and is consumable by the runtime team to gate optimizations.
A6: Canary rollout playbook documented with explicit fallback mapping (if optimized variant fails, route to compatible fallback variant/version within same profile family).
A7: Telemetry: each catalog entry records profile, ingest result code, and rolling quality eval (basic perplexity and hallucination signal) for the first 72 hours after public exposure.
A8: PM/Design review of catalog UI changes (profile selector, lifecycle state) completed and PR merged to catalog repo.
A9: Security review completed for Tier-1 community submissions; ticket for full provenance enforcement created for later cycle.
A10: Migration path: for existing unprofiled catalog entries, a one-time automated classification report is generated and owners are notified to confirm or override.
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for manifest parser and validator. 2) Integration test where a golden Tier-0 artifact is ingested and served; observe fallback behavior when KV cache is intentionally disabled. 3) Canary: select three community models to progress through trial->soft-pinned->pinned with synthetic traffic and synthetic eval prompt set; capture latency, OOMs, and error rates. 4) Regression: run catalog e2e smoke suite against a pinned variant and its fallback to verify deterministic outputs for canonical prompts.
notes:
- Introduced the phrase 'profile' to reduce binary pinned/unpinned decisions. Profiles are intentionally conservative for Tier-0/1 to prioritize availability over aggressive optimizations.
- For quantization compatibility we will annotate recommended quantization tiers (e.g., q4_0,q8_1) but runtime will still enforce safeties at execution time.
- Owners: Add a single 'catalog_contact' field to model_manifest to accelerate rollback and communications.
